reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: AI in education and learning
themes.definition: AI discussed as transforming teaching and learning, including national education programs and responsible child-centred learning.
themes.inclusion: Include passages on AI in schools, teacher/student support, AI education programs or skills to use AI.
themes.exclusion: Exclude general education references without AI.
themes.boundary_cases: National AI education programs (e.g., AI Leap) are coded here and also AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY.

examples.quote: Artificial intelligence should empower teaching and learning rather than replace them.
Therefore, Estonia is making a new leap, the artificial intelligence leap.

themes.label: National AI programs and experience sharing
themes.definition: Speaker showcases own national AI/digital initiatives and offers them as best practice to others.
themes.inclusion: Include descriptions of national AI programs or national digital success reinforced by AI, and offers to share this experience.
themes.exclusion: Exclude purely global calls without national reference.
themes.boundary_cases: Sharing experience via UN bodies may also be AI_UN_ROLE or AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING.

examples.quote: digitalization which has now been reinforced by AI, has enabled our small country to grow, innovate, and connect globally

themes.label: Leadership in UN AI processes
themes.definition: References to UN AI processes and bodies, such as co-chairing the Global Dialogue on AI Governance or AI for Good, and working through UNICEF/ITU.
themes.inclusion: Include mentions of UN-specific AI bodies, dialogues, commissions or agencies as venues for AI work.
themes.exclusion: Exclude generic multilateralism without an AI link.
themes.boundary_cases: Candidacies for UN tech posts framed around digital transformation count only if linked to AI or digital inclusion.

examples.quote: As a co-chair of the first UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance, alongside with El Salvador

themes.label: AI serving dignity and human rights
themes.definition: AI must be used wisely and responsibly in service of dignity, development, human rights and humanity.
themes.inclusion: Include passages insisting AI serve human rights, dignity or humanity, or be used responsibly.
themes.exclusion: Exclude human rights content that makes no reference to AI or digital rights.
themes.boundary_cases: Statements acknowledging AI risks but expressing confidence it can serve humanity may also be AI_OPPORTUNITY_RISK_DUALITY.

examples.quote: They must serve dignity, development, and human rights, not the other way around.
Like any new technology, AI poses risks and brings challenges. But with knowledge, wisdom and unity, we can put it to use in the service of humanity.

themes.label: No country left behind digitally
themes.definition: Ensuring AI and digital benefits reach all countries and communities equally.
themes.inclusion: Include statements aiming for AI benefits to reach many countries or ensure equal opportunities and no one left behind.
themes.boundary_cases: Connectivity-only statements without AI are borderline; include when in an AI-context passage.

examples.quote: assure that no country is left behind in the digital transformation
ensuring that AI creates equal opportunities for all humanity

value.rationale: Estonia's passages center on AI in education (AI Leap), national digital experience shared via UN bodies, and human-rights-anchored, inclusive AI; the 2026 closing passage is general digital multilateralism.
